title: A variable defined inside an iterator is evaluated in each row, with the context transition of the measure it holds
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", SUMX ( Customer, VAR S = [Sales Amount] RETURN IF ( S > 100, S ) ) )

source.quote: Using a variable ensures that the evaluation happens only once, and that the DAX engine does not choose an execution plan requiring multiple evaluations of Sales Amount
source.supports: the CustomerSales variable defined inside SUMX ( Customer, ... ) holds the sales of the customer being iterated

source.quote: Variables are evaluated in the filter context where they are defined, and their evaluation happens at most once.
source.supports: a variable is evaluated where it is defined, not where it is used

derivation: Per customer: Ann rows 1, 2, 7 = 100 + 40 + 100 = 240; Bob rows 3, 4 = 20 + 50 = 70; Cho rows 5, 6 = 200 + 30 = 230; Dee has no sales, BLANK. S > 100 holds for Ann and Cho only (BLANK > 100 is FALSE); the two-argument IF gives BLANK for the others, and SUMX skips blanks: 240 + 230 = 470.
